8:["$","$L83",null,{"children":["$","$84",null,{"name":"Next.MetadataOutlet","children":"$@85"}]}]
9:["$","p","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Before spending $500 or more on a standing desk, a fair question: do they actually improve anything?"}}]
a:["$","p","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"The research is more nuanced than the marketing suggests. Standing desks don't burn significantly more calories than sitting — the difference is roughly 8 calories per hour. What they <em>do</em> change is posture variability. The problem with sitting all day isn't sitting itself — it's holding any single static position for hours. A standing desk gives you a way to alternate positions, which reduces the lower back compression, hip flexor tightening, and shoulder rounding that comes from locked-in sitting."}}]
b:["$","p","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Studies published in the <em>Occupational and Environmental Medicine</em> journal found that workers with sit-stand desks reported 54% less upper back and neck pain after four weeks. A separate trial in <em>BMC Public Health</em> found meaningful reductions in fatigue and improved mood — though not from standing per se, but from breaking up seated time."}}]
c:["$","p","4",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"The practical conclusion: a standing desk works if you actually use it to alternate. If you stand all day you'll develop different problems (varicose veins, foot pain, lower back fatigue from a different angle). The goal is movement — alternating between sitting and standing every 45–60 minutes."}}]
d:["$","p","5",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"This guide covers the <strong>best standing desks in 2026</strong> — electric and manual — across six price points, plus exactly what specs matter and what the marketing doesn't tell you."}}]
e:["$","h2","6",{"id":"what-to-look-for-before-you-buy","children":"What to Look For Before You Buy"}]
f:["$","h3","7",{"id":"stability-first","children":"Stability First"}]
10:["$","p","8",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"The single most important and most commonly faked spec in standing desk reviews is stability. A wobble at standing height makes typing uncomfortable, causes monitor shake during video calls, and signals a frame that will degrade faster under daily use."}}]
11:["$","p","9",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"How to evaluate stability without testing it:"}}]
12:["$","ul","10",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Cross-bracing</strong> — desks with X-braces or H-frames between the two legs are more rigid than those without"}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Leg wall thickness</strong> — look for 3mm or thicker steel on the leg column. Budget desks use 2mm; it feels hollow and wobbles"}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Single-stage vs. two-stage vs. three-stage legs</strong> — three-stage legs (three telescoping segments) reach lower floor heights and taller heights but wobble more than two-stage at the same width. Two-stage legs are more rigid for typical 27–47 inch height ranges"}}],["$","li","3",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Weight</strong> — heavier frames are almost always more stable. Under 50 lbs is a red flag for a full-size electric desk"}}]]}]
13:["$","h3","11",{"id":"height-range","children":"Height Range"}]
14:["$","p","12",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Your seated desk height should put your elbows at 90° with relaxed shoulders. Standing height should do the same — meaning the desk height range must span from your seated elbow height to your standing elbow height."}}]
15:["$","p","13",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"A rough formula: <strong>seated height = your height × 0.43</strong>. <strong>Standing height = your height × 0.62</strong>."}}]
16:["$","p","14",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"For a 5'6\" user that's roughly 28\" seated and 41\" standing. Most electric desks cover 24–49 inches, which handles users from 4'10\" to 6'6\". If you're particularly tall or short, verify the exact range before buying."}}]
17:["$","h3","15",{"id":"motor-and-lifting-capacity","children":"Motor and Lifting Capacity"}]
18:["$","p","16",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Single-motor desks</strong> use one motor driving both legs via a central drive shaft. Cheaper but more prone to uneven leg movement over time. Fine for loads under 30 lbs."}}]
19:["$","p","17",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Dual-motor desks</strong> have one motor per leg, synchronized electronically. More reliable for heavy setups — dual monitors, large monitors, desktop computers on the desk. Spec 150 lbs or higher lifting capacity if you run a heavy dual-monitor workstation."}}]
1a:["$","p","18",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Noise level</strong> matters more than most buyers anticipate. A motor that hits 50 dB in an open-plan home (or worse, during a video call) becomes an annoyance within a week. Look for motors rated under 45 dB — the best are quieter than a normal conversation."}}]
1b:["$","h3","19",{"id":"desktop-surface","children":"Desktop Surface"}]
1c:["$","p","20",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"The frame is where the engineering lives, but the desktop is what you actually interact with. Key considerations:"}}]
1d:["$","ul","21",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Thickness</strong> — 1\" (25mm) laminate tops feel hollow and bounce under heavy typing. 1.25\" or thicker feels solid"}}],["$","li","1",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Material</strong> — MDF core is standard; solid wood costs more but is denser and more rigid. Bamboo is an excellent value: hard, sustainable, and dimensionally stable"}}],["$","li","2",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Size</strong> — most people underestimate how much surface area they need. A 60\"×30\" surface is the minimum comfortable size for a dual-monitor plus laptop setup. 72\" if you want elbow room"}}]]}]

6b:["$","p","99",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"A standing desk only helps if it's at the right height. Use this setup sequence:"}}]
6c:["$","ol","100",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Set seated height first.</strong> Sit in your chair with feet flat on the floor, back straight. 6d:["$","ol","101",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Set standing height.</strong> Stand in the shoes you normally wear at your desk — this matters, especially for women who switch between flats and heels. Adjust the desk until your forearms again rest at 90–110°. Elbows slightly relaxed, shoulders down. Record this height."}}]]}]
6e:["$","ol","102",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Program both as presets.</strong> You want zero friction switching between positions. If you have to think about the height, you'll stop using it."}}]]}]

70:["$","ol","104",{"children":[["$","li","0",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Set a timer.</strong> The science suggests changing position every 45–60 minutes. 71:["$","h2","105",{"id":"frequently-asked-questions","children":"Frequently Asked Questions"}]
72:["$","p","106",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>How long should I stand at my standing desk each day?</strong>"}}]
73:["$","p","107",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Research suggests 2–4 hours of standing spread across an 8-hour workday is the sweet spot. More than 4 hours of continuous standing causes its own problems. The goal is variation — sit, stand, move — not replacing sitting with standing."}}]
74:["$","p","108",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Do I need a mat for standing?</strong>"}}]
75:["$","p","109",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Yes, if you stand for more than 30 minutes at a time. Without a mat, the fatigue accumulates in your feet, calves, and lower back within 20–30 minutes. Anti-fatigue mats (the Topo by Ergodriven, the Standee by AmazonBasics, or any gel-core mat) extend comfortable standing time significantly."}}]
76:["$","p","110",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Will a standing desk help my back pain?</strong>"}}]
77:["$","p","111",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"For <em>lower back pain from prolonged sitting</em>, yes — the research is reasonably clear that alternating positions reduces compressive load on the lumbar discs. For other sources of back pain (structural issues, disc herniation, scoliosis), a standing desk alone won't solve it. Consult a physiotherapist before assuming a desk purchase is the fix."}}]
78:["$","p","112",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Can I put a monitor arm on any standing desk?</strong>"}}]
79:["$","p","113",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Yes, as long as the desktop is thick enough to clamp to and the desk's lifting capacity accounts for the arm and monitor weight. Most 1.25\" or thicker desktops accept monitor arm clamps. Grommet mounts require drilling a 2.5\" hole — check if your desktop allows modifications before buying."}}]
7a:["$","p","114",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>Is a standing desk worth it if I work from home?</strong>"}}]
7b:["$","p","115",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"If you work 6+ hours at a desk daily, yes — the ergonomic and energy benefits are real and accumulate over months and years. If you work 3 hours or less, a good ergonomic chair will likely deliver more benefit per dollar. The standing desk ROI scales with hours spent at the desk."}}]
7c:["$","p","116",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"<strong>What size desktop do I need?</strong>"}}]

7e:["$","p","118",{"dangerouslySetInnerHTML":{"__html":"Most people underestimate by one size. When in doubt, go larger — you can always use the space, you can't unchoose a desk that feels cramped."}}]
